question:
(a) Compare the temperature dependence of resistivity of metals and semiconductors.
(b) Explain why the resistivity of a semiconductor decreases when temperature increases.
(c) Mention the sign of temperature coefficient of resistivity for a semiconductor.

options.A:
(a) Resistivity of both metals and semiconductors increases with temperature.
(b) Semiconductor resistivity increases because charge carriers decrease.
(c) The temperature coefficient for semiconductors is positive.
options.B:
(a) Resistivity of metals decreases and that of semiconductors increases with temperature.
(b) Semiconductor resistivity decreases because lattice vibrations decrease.
(c) The temperature coefficient is zero.
options.C:
(a) Metal resistivity increases with temperature because electron-ion collisions increase, whereas semiconductor resistivity decreases because charge-carrier concentration increases.
(b) More thermally generated carriers increase conductivity; since $\rho=1/\sigma$, semiconductor resistivity decreases.
(c) A semiconductor has negative temperature coefficient of resistivity.
options.D:
(a) Metal and semiconductor resistivities are independent of temperature.
(b) Semiconductor resistivity decreases because free electrons stop colliding.
(c) The temperature coefficient is positive.
